title: ESA releases Copernicus Sentinel-3 image of West Antarctica
excerpt: The satellite imagery captures the sea ice extent near the Antarctic Peninsula as the southern hemisphere winter concludes.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency released an image of West Antarctica captured by the Copernicus Sentinel-3 satellite on 30 September 2026. The image displays an area of approximately 1200 km by 1700 km, covering the periphery of the continent.

According to the European Space Agency, the imagery shows sea ice engulfing the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula and parts of the Weddell Sea. The National Snow and Ice Data Center reported that Antarctic sea ice likely reached its annual maximum extent on 14 September 2026.

Elephant Island, which is about 50 km in length, is visible against ice-free ocean on the left-hand side of the image. It is located about 930 km from the tip of Argentina’s Tierra del Fuego.

The image reveals a variety of textures reflecting different types of ice, including areas of tightly packed sea ice on the right. Large floes comparable in size to Elephant Island are visible, progressing to smaller pieces of sea ice that form swirling shapes in the ocean.
